title: Required factors in an agency’s authorizing statute
shortTitle: Required factors in an agency’s authorizing statute
summary: An agency’s authorizing statute can require analysis additional to the APA’s general procedures.
notes: An authorizing or organic statute defines the agency’s powers and may require findings or consideration of particular effects. Section 706 review helps enforce those requirements: ignoring a factor Congress required can make a rule arbitrary and capricious and contrary to law. The notes describe Public Citizen v. FMCSA, where the agency failed to consider truck drivers’ health; Owner-Operator Independent Drivers, concerning driver harassment from recording equipment; and Chamber of Commerce v. SEC, concerning required analysis of regulatory costs. These short examples identify the significance of the omissions; they are not full briefs of the underlying litigation.
